tooling: hand-reviewed triage; method and evidence in docs/DECISIONS.md (2026-10-05: image hardening)

statements.impact_statement: The flaw is in systemd-homed. Only the libsystemd0/libudev1 client libraries (dependencies of apt/util-linux) are installed; systemd-homed is not in the image and there is no init system.

The flaw is in the header-only binary-heap priority-queue template (erase_if). Template code is compiled into consumers; the shared runtime libraries (libstdc++6, libgcc-s1, libatomic1) do not contain it, no libstdc++ headers are installed, and no binary in the image is built from that container.

statements.status_notes: Integer overflow in libstdc++'s aligned operator new. The C++ consumers are HarfBuzz/Pango (WeasyPrint report rendering) and, in the worker, OpenSCAP. Whether an attacker-sized aligned allocation is reachable from report data has not been established; tracking the Debian fix.

statements.impact_statement: Requires a caller of strfmon/strfmon_l. No ELF object in the image imports either symbol (checked with nm -D across the exported filesystem); CPython's locale.currency is pure Python.
Requires a caller of the deprecated ns_printrr/ns_printrrf/fp_nquery resolver printers. No ELF object in the image imports them (nm -D across the exported filesystem).

The flaw is in mount(8)'s X-mount.* helper/post-hook handling and needs a privileged mount invocation (SUID mount or CAP_SYS_ADMIN). The mount package is purged from both images. No process in the image executes it: the API runs only its Python entrypoints, the worker additionally trivy, grype, clairctl, cosign, skopeo, oscap/oscap-chroot and zstd. As deployed by the chart every container drops all capabilities and has a read-only root filesystem; the scap-worker Deployment runs the worker image as root but adds back only CHOWN/FOWNER/DAC_OVERRIDE/FSETID/SETFCAP/SYS_CHROOT (no SYS_ADMIN); libmount's mount context is never driven.

No process in the image executes it: the API runs only its Python entrypoints, the worker additionally trivy, grype, clairctl, cosign, skopeo, oscap/oscap-chroot and zstd. The overflow is in the infocmp command-line program (progs/infocmp.c), not in the ncurses libraries. infocmp is never executed; the containers have no TTY and no terminfo input.
Pod::Text is shipped in perl-modules, which is not installed; perl-base in the image contains no Pod/Text.pm.
Archive::Tar is shipped in perl-modules, which is not installed; perl-base in the image contains no Archive/Tar.pm.

Requires a privileged process applying libacl pathname functions to an attacker-controlled path. The only libacl consumers are coreutils/sed/tar, which the API never executes (its only child process is `python -m posture.report_worker`); it runs as uid 10001 without capabilities.

The system libexpat1 is used only by libfontconfig1 to parse the image's root-owned /etc/fonts configuration. CPython's pyexpat (xml.etree) is built against its bundled expat (2.8.5), not this package; no other ELF object in either image imports XML_ParserCreate (nm -D), so request or scanned-image data never reaches the Debian libexpat.

Requires gzprintf/gzvprintf after a non-blocking gzwrite stall. No ELF object in either image imports gzprintf or gzvprintf (nm -D across the exported filesystems); the gzwrite users (libxml2, librpmio, libapt-pkg, dpkg-deb) write regular files, never non-blocking descriptors.

libcurl's only consumer in the worker is libopenscap (nm -D: no other importer of curl_easy_perform), which uses it solely for --fetch-remote-resources. The worker never passes that flag (posture.scap.oscap builds the argv); SCAP content is fetched by the Python worker and sha256-checked. skopeo/trivy/grype/cosign/clairctl are static Go binaries that do not use libcurl.

Requires installing or rebuilding a source RPM. librpm is used read-only by OpenSCAP's rpminfo probe to iterate the scanned image's rpmdb; nothing installs or rebuilds packages.
Requires querying a package manifest file (rpm -q -p). The rpm CLI is not installed and the rpminfo probe only iterates the rpmdb; no package or manifest files are opened.

statements.status_notes: Header-parsing flaw. The rpmdb of a scanned RHEL/UBI image is untrusted input to OpenSCAP's rpminfo probe (scap-worker); whether the probe's header reads reach the affected tag handling is not yet established. Mitigations: probes run chrooted into a scratch copy, the scap-worker is a separate, short-lived pod.

statements.impact_statement: The flaw is in libxml2's Python bindings (python3-libxml2), which are not installed.

statements.status_notes: libxml2 (via libopenscap/libxslt/libxmlsec1) parses SCAP content, which is sha256-pinned, and, through OVAL xmlfilecontent probes, XML files inside the scanned image, which are untrusted. Reachability of the affected functions from those probes is being assessed; tracking the Debian fix.

libopenscap (acl_extended_file) and librpm (acl_get_file) call libacl on paths inside the scanned image's rootfs, and the scap-worker runs those probes with CAP_SYS_CHROOT. Probes are chrooted into a scratch copy of the rootfs; whether symlink substitution can escape that is being assessed.

statements.impact_statement: grype links only the moby client/API packages of github.com/docker/docker (to read images from a daemon, which the worker never has). The AuthZ-plugin request handling is daemon code and is not compiled into the binary.

Daemon-side flaw in github.com/docker/docker (engine archive upload / docker cp mount setup). grype links only the moby client/API packages; the engine code is not compiled into the binary, and the worker has no Docker daemon or socket.
